title: Household Add-On Membership: basis for the recurring dues charge each billing cycle
content:
## Product and scope
This document states the Household Add-On Membership basis for charging the tier's recurring monthly dues, and the status the add-on's record must show before any recurring or late-fee charge may be recorded against it.

## Rule
Each billing cycle, the add-on is charged its tier's monthly dues as a recurring charge, billed on that tier's billing-cycle alignment. A recurring dues charge, or a late-fee charge on that same add-on, may be recorded in the system only while the add-on's record shows a status of active or suspended.

## Eligibility: which add-on records may be charged
- Applicable event: a recurring dues charge, or a one-time late-fee charge, being recorded against a household add-on.
- Authority: the add-on's status is read from the system's own record of that add-on, not from anything the customer states on the call.
- Object correlation: the status checked is the status of the specific add-on record the charge is being recorded against.
- Allowed statuses: active or suspended. A charge may not be recorded against an add-on whose record shows applied (not yet activated) or closed.

## Points of judgement
- An add-on's applied status (before its first activation charge) and its closed status (after removal) both fall outside the allowed range; no recurring or late-fee charge may be recorded in either state.
- The suspended status is explicitly included in the allowed range, so a suspended add-on continues to be capable of being charged (for example, the late fee that follows a failed collection) even though it is not currently active.

## Boundary case (illustrative only)
An add-on whose record currently shows suspended may still have a late-fee charge recorded against it, because suspended is one of the two allowed statuses. An add-on whose record shows closed may not have any further recurring or late-fee charge recorded against it, because closed is not one of the two allowed statuses.

The tier's own monthly dues rate is recorded in that tier's own parameter basis.
